correctness.rationale: The finite two-target path has a well-defined Markov cutting process. Conditioning on a uniform cut proves the one-target inactive-arm recurrence F_c(d)=z(c+1+sum_{h<d}F_c(h))/(c+d+1), and the product Q_c(d)=(c+1)prod_{k=c+1}^{c+d}(1+z/k). First-cut conditioning for two targets then yields z^{-1}E[z^S]=prod_{k=a+1}^{N-1}(k+z)/(k+1)+prod_{k=b+1}^{N-1}(k+z)/(k+1)-1, with complete telescoping and exact endpoint conditions. Coefficientwise subtraction proves the signed error and both exact total-variation constants a/N, b/N. Harmonic sums and Taylor remainders give the interior PGF and normalized mixture; probability masses sum to one. For a/N→0 the TV error a/N vanishes, auxiliary independent Bernoulli variance diverges and is asymptotic to H_N-H_{a+1}, and Lindeberg plus TV proves the CLT. An independent exact-rational Markov recursion checks 55 cases (3≤N≤12), 964 assertions, in the bundled verify_path_cutting.py; finite tests do not substitute for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Moving the source relative to the two terminal targets changes the natural geometric balance in an established random separation model. The all-arm finite PGF and sharp exact TV errors do more than restate a symmetric continuum limit; they characterize the full stopping distribution and identify a quantifiable, not merely heuristic, reduction to an independent-Bernoulli count. The resulting tight asymmetric positive-Poisson mixtures and boundary Gaussian crossover answer a structural scaling question, and the finite TV identity determines exactly when a one-arm proxy is accurate. The boundary regime is motivated by varying source placement, not an arbitrary unmotivated statistic.
